items.title: Document service and secure object storage flows
acceptanceCriteria: Direct-upload intents validate the declared document class, content type and size before a signed upload URL is issued; finalization validates the stored object's actual size and magic-number content type before metadata registration, DOCUMENT_UPLOADED publication, or clean-download eligibility
Tenant-scoped signed access and document metadata are audited

evidence.note: The first criterion was corrected on acceptance because it contradicted the approved architecture it was meant to describe. ADR-014 has the client PUT straight to private object storage, so bytes reach storage before this platform can read them: no validation of "real content type" can precede that by construction. What the platform actually guarantees is two checks at two moments — declared class, type and size before a credential is issued, and the stored object's actual size and magic-number type before it is registered, announced or downloadable. No scope or estimate changed; COM-004 remains 13 points.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service exec jest --selectProjects integration -t 'what the bytes actually are'
evidence.note: The corrected criterion, proven on real bytes in real storage: an HTML page uploaded as a PDF, an executable whatever it is called, a real file of the wrong type for its class, an empty object and a finalize with nothing uploaded are all refused. The declared/detected mismatch is reported as a mismatch rather than silently corrected, and the size persisted is the one storage reports.

evidence.ref: pnpm --filter @rasta/document-service exec jest --selectProjects integration -t 'what the boundary refuses'
evidence.note: The pre-credential half: an unknown document class, a content type the class does not permit and a declared size over the class limit are each refused before any upload URL exists, and an unknown field is refused rather than dropped.

The second criterion: another organization's document is reported absent rather than forbidden, receives no download URL and cannot be deleted; listings are scoped; the oversight role and roles with no document business are refused outright. Every state change is recorded — DOCUMENT_UPLOADED, DOCUMENT_SCANNED, DOCUMENT_DELETED and VIRUS_DETECTED carry the actor and correlation id through the transactional outbox, and deletion is a tombstone the database refuses to accept without an actor, time and reason.

evidence.note: NTF-001: the first acceptance criterion is met — domain events produce idempotent in-app notifications, deduplicated on content with the daysRemaining banding of ADR-054
NTF-002: read API and write-once read state, enforced in the database rather than in the service
Green on main at a84269a; 180 unit and 70 integration tests for this service

BLOCKED, not READY, for two reasons. (1) The second acceptance criterion has no implementation: services/notification-service/src has no channel, mail or email module at all, and Q-37 — which email provider — is an open blocking question. (2) NTF-002 publishes no domain event for read or dismiss, so audit-service never observes either action; closing that deviation is a product-owner decision, still open on 2026-09-18.

Blocker (2) is closed. notification-service now publishes NOTIFICATION_READ, NOTIFICATION_DISMISSED and NOTIFICATION_ALL_READ from a transactional outbox, in the same transaction as the state change and only when a row actually moved, and audit-service subscribes to rasta.notification.v1. ADR-054 § 3 offered two ways out and the written exception was rejected: S-06 is a security rule, and a documented exception lowers the platform audit floor permanently. Blocker (1) stands — there is still no channel, mail or email module, and Q-37 is open.

NTF-003: notification preferences with the five-layer precedence ladder (MANDATORY_POLICY, RULE, CATEGORY, GLOBAL, CHANNEL_DEFAULT), a reversible migration, and the GET /v1/preferences/effective endpoint that returns the winning layer. Q-38 was answered and implemented in the same change as per-rule mandatoryChannels. Quiet hours were deliberately deferred to NTF-004 and the deviation is recorded in the ADR-054 implementation plan.
Green for NTF-003 before merge at e6d509e.

The first piece of NTF-004, and only that piece: a MailChannel port with a closed set of failure reasons, an SMTP adapter that refuses header injection and a second recipient before a socket opens, SMTP 4xx/5xx retry classification, and an integration suite against a real Mailpit. Three independent locks keep it from reaching a human: the shipped sender is an RFC 2606 .invalid address, deliversToRealRecipients is a constant in app.module.ts rather than a setting, and env.spec.ts asserts that no environment variable matching REAL_RECIPIENT|PRODUCTION_MAIL|MAIL_ENABLED|SEND_REAL exists.
All seven jobs green on the merge ref of #63, including integration and the economic end-to-end path.

Status on 2026-09-21: blocker (1) of the 2026-09-18 note is closed — the channel module now exists. What remains of COM-008 is unbuilt work, not a blocker: Persian RTL templates, retry and backoff, suppression, the NOTIFICATION_SENT and NOTIFICATION_FAILED events, delivery-outcome recording, and the quiet hours deferred from NTF-003. Whether COM-008 may be ACCEPTED while Q-37 (which email provider, which sender identity) is still open is a product-owner decision and is not assumed here.

NTF-004 in full: the EMAIL channel value together with the worker that writes it, two template tables whose published versions are immutable and are seeded from the code catalogue, Persian right-to-left rendering with Persian digits and Hijri-Shamsi dates in the recipient timezone, the quiet hours NTF-003 deferred with two new endpoints, a claim-based mail worker on the 1s/5s/30s/2m/10m ladder with jitter, and NOTIFICATION_SENT and NOTIFICATION_FAILED published from the outbox in the same transaction as the outcome.

Six cases against a real PostgreSQL and a real Mailpit, asserted through Mailpit HTTP API rather than the adapter return value: sent and recorded and announced once; Persian right-to-left with a Jalali date on the wire; a dead port retried and announced to nobody; the ladder ending in DEAD with exactly one NOTIFICATION_FAILED; a quiet window holding a message without spending an attempt; and a published template version whose text changed refusing to seed. 279 unit and 120 integration tests pass locally.

Three named deviations, none hidden: the per-channel circuit breaker and outbound rate limit of ADR-054 section 7 are not built and are not in the acceptance criteria; quiet hours live in their own table rather than as columns on notification_preference, because that table holds one row per scope and the ADR shape allowed one person three contradictory windows for one channel; and the two read-only template diagnostic endpoints are deferred to NTF-005.

Q-37 remains open and all three locks hold: deliversToRealRecipients is a constant false in app.module.ts, the shipped sender is an RFC 2606 .invalid address, and env.spec.ts proves no environment variable matching REAL_RECIPIENT|PRODUCTION_MAIL|MAIL_ENABLED|SEND_REAL exists. No email has reached a real person. Whether COM-008 may be ACCEPTED while the procurement half of Q-37 — which provider, which domain, which sender identity — is unanswered is a product-owner decision and is not assumed here.

CI evidence gap closed (Codex acceptance audit of 2026-10-23): Mailpit runs as a pinned service container in both integration jobs and REQUIRE_MAILPIT=1 makes the email-delivery and mail-channel specs fail rather than skip when it is unreachable; the quiet-hours case now pins the worker clock. Merge commit e8286f2, merged 2026-10-23.

ACCEPTED by the Product Owner (the repository owner), 2026-10-23, in the project-manager chat, on the evidence above, the Codex acceptance audit of 2026-10-23 and its re-check on PR #365 (both criteria met: idempotent in-app notifications from domain events; email that respects preferences and records the delivery outcome, asserted in CI against a real Mailpit). items.title: Identity, organization, asset, fleet and maintenance web surfaces
acceptanceCriteria: Core operational workflows are usable at documented permissions
Desktop and supported mobile viewports pass accessibility and tenant-isolation E2E

evidence.note: The portal runs the OIDC flow on its own server: no access token and no refresh token ever reaches browser JavaScript. Written because docs/16 contradicted itself — section 16.1 named a browser library and section 16.11 required the refresh token in an HttpOnly cookie, which a browser library cannot write. The rule won and the tool changed.

The session and the shell: the OIDC flow in Next.js route handlers with PKCE, state and nonce; an AES-256-GCM sealed session cookie that is HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict; a server-side gateway client that refuses any origin but the gateway; /login; and a dashboard that shows the signed-in person, their active organization and their effective roles, fetched through the gateway on the server.

67 server tests: the session cookie refuses a tampered, foreign-key, truncated or stale-shaped value and leaves no token readable; PKCE derives S256 correctly; the id token is refused for a wrong nonce, a wrong audience and a wrong key; the gateway client refuses a service port, another host and another port, and never fetches when it refuses; and the identity schema drops the email and phone identity returns. 354 portal tests in total.

The first browser job in this repository, running against a production build in CI as apps/web/playwright.config.ts said it would from EXP-001. It asserts only what a browser can: the document is served dir=rtl lang=fa, the way in works with JavaScript disabled, and localStorage and sessionStorage are both empty — which is ADR-059 central claim, provable only here.

Still unbuilt, and not claimed: /organizations, /assets, /assets/[id], /drivers, /usage, /maintenance and /maintenance/[id]. EXP-002 is not finished by this change; its first acceptance criterion — core operational workflows usable at documented permissions — needs those screens.

The first two operational screens: /assets, with filters and cursor paging carried entirely in the URL so a filtered list is a link somebody can send, and /assets/[id], the electronic dossier — identity, every compliance blocker rather than the first, costs, and recent activity. Both are fetched on the server through the gateway and both are pure functions of the read result.

Fourteen screen tests covering the states a developer never reaches by accident: a filter that matched nothing worded differently from a tenant with no assets, a forbidden read rendered as a refusal, an outage rendered with its correlation id, an unknown status shown as it arrived rather than hidden, and a missing asset answered exactly as another tenant’s asset is. Both screens pass jest-axe.

Nine server tests: only the filters the caller set reach the gateway, the asset id is percent-encoded into the path rather than interpolated, every compliance blocker survives, money stays a string, and the coordinate, document references and raw event detail in the dossier response are all dropped before anything can render them.

The write path and the first screen that uses it: a CSRF token bound to the sealed session and checked before any gateway call, a server-minted submission id sent as Idempotency-Key and as clientReference, service validation details mapped back onto the field that caused them, and a plain form post to a server action so the whole thing works with JavaScript disabled. /usage is the proof.

Seventeen tests on the order the handler enforces: no session, no CSRF token, a token from another session, a stale token after a re-login, and a submission id the server did not mint each refuse with nothing called. Two posts of one form carry one client reference; two renders carry two. Nothing token-shaped appears in the state the page renders.

What reaches the wire and what comes back: the Idempotency-Key header, the refusal of any origin but the gateway, a 400 detail landing on its field, a message the portal knows translated and one it does not shown as it arrived, a 422 business rule kept as a sentence, and a 5xx body never read at all.

Still unbuilt and not claimed: /organizations, /drivers, and the maintenance and asset write paths. EXP-002 is not finished by this change; what it adds is the foundation every later form inherits, proven by one screen.

/organizations — سازمان و اعضا: the organization's own profile (the three fields organization-service accepts), the member list, each member's roles, and revoking a membership. The role picker renders the caller's own grantable set, which identity-service computes from the configured ladder and now returns on GET /v1/users/me — so the form offers exactly what the service would accept rather than a hardcoded list that drifts when ROLE_GRANTS_BY_* changes. Hierarchy management is deliberately absent: docs/16 § 16.6 puts it on the admin console's own /organizations for UNION_ADMIN, and apps/admin does not exist yet.

45 tests on the screen and its three write paths: every gate refusal proves the service was not called, the role picker renders only grantable roles and preserves a held role the caller cannot grant instead of silently stripping it, an empty ladder is stated rather than shown as an empty form, and the ladder refusal from identity-service is rendered as its own outcome with a correlation id. Two jest-axe passes. 666 portal tests in total.

A defect the member work found in shared code: callGateway always parsed the body as JSON, so a 204 No Content — which POST /v1/memberships/:id/revoke answers — threw after the service had already done the work, reporting a successful revocation as a failure. Fixed and covered three ways.

EXT-005 is the follow-up that closes it for the dangerous direction: a gateway revocation list fed by the events identity-service already publishes. Filed under EP-EXPANSION because the window was accepted for MVP, so the fix is post-MVP, and the backlog has no post-MVP hardening epic; EP-EXPANSION's 'before national scale' is the nearest honest home. Whether a dedicated hardening epic is wanted is a backlog-structure decision left to the project manager.
changeLog.approvalRef: Project manager decision on ADR-060, 2026-09-24 (PR #84)
